title: Soticlestat in WWOX research
summary: Retain as a CYP46A1 research comparator once local 24S-hydroxycholesterol (24S-HC) depletion is verified. Defer pediatric WWOX trial priority.

graph.evidence: Mouse enzyme occupancy precedes the drop in bulk brain oxysterol.
graph.inference: An acute circuit test can occur before the proposed mediator changes.
graph.hypothesis: A local 24S-HC excess sustains late NMDA-dependent recruitment.
graph.experiment: Verify local depletion and test whether metabolite add-back reverses the late effect.

evidence: At 1 h after one exposure, apparent mouse CYP46A1 occupancy was 99.1% and brain 24S-HC was 107.4% of vehicle. At 24 h these were 35.2% and 67.4% (three animals per time).
After the fifth exposure, 63.0–74.3% of control 24S-HC remained. Figure 4 and Table S2 give a 25.7–37.0% reduction. Results prose reports about 60% reduction.
inference: An acute assay can precede the change in metabolite. WWOX models differ in CYP46A1 RNA direction. Local 24S-HC is unmeasured.
hypothesis: A local cortical 24S-HC excess could sustain late NMDA-dependent recruitment in WWOX.
experiment: In age-matched cortex, verify local depletion and test reversal by 24S-HC add-back at fixed soticlestat exposure. Measure early recruitment and inhibition separately. Verified depletion without a selective late effect lowers priority.
limits: Dravet and Lennox–Gastaut phase 3 studies missed their primary endpoints despite large plasma 24S-HC falls. WOREE efficacy, local exposure and infant tolerability remain unresolved.

sources.label: Miyamoto et al., Figure 4 and Supplemental Table 2C–D
Breton et al., juvenile Wwox-deficient cortical physiology
